sentences.text: Angulomastacator, meaning "bend chewer," is a duck-billed dinosaur known only from a partial left upper jaw bone. This fossilized maxilla is curved down by approximately 45 degrees at the front, a feature unique among hadrosaurs.

The genus belongs to the lambeosaurine group of hadrosaurs, which are characterized by hollow cranial crests, and is classified within the family Hadrosauridae, subfamily Lambeosaurinae, and possibly the tribe Lambeosaurini.
The front of its upper jaw bone curves down by approximately 45 degrees, a shape not seen in other duck-billed dinosaurs.
Evidence suggests the animal died during a flooding event, as its remains show signs of transport by water.

The fossil was found in the upper shale member of the Aguja Formation within deposits interpreted as a small tributary channel. The species was formally described as the new taxon Angulomastacator daviesi in 2009 by Lehman and Wagner.

Angulomastacator lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77 million years ago, in what is now North America. The time range for the genus is recorded as Campanian, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that the unique characteristics of the maxilla support the hypothesis that the dinosaurs of the Aguja Formation were endemic forms.
